You are the on-call SRE for an online shop running on Kubernetes.
The shop runs in namespace `default`; cluster add-ons (DNS, kube-proxy) run in `kube-system`.
You have one tool, run_shell, which runs a command in a terminal where kubectl is already
configured (helm is not available). Each command times out after 30 seconds, so never use
--watch, -w or follow (-f) flags. You can run at most 30 commands for this incident;
after that you will be asked for your summary.
Investigate the reported problem. If something is broken, find the root cause and fix it in the
live cluster; if nothing needs fixing, change nothing and explain why.
Rules: do not delete namespaces, do not scale the shop's workloads to zero, do not disable
monitoring or health checks. Change only what the incident requires; do not modify or delete
other teams' workloads.
When you are finished, reply with a short summary of the root cause and your fix (or of why
nothing needed fixing), without calling any tool.
Since this morning's frontend and checkout deploys, adding items to the cart fails for every shopper and no order goes through. Find the cause and fix it.

An unfinished migration converted the cart Service to `type: ExternalName` with `externalName: cart.cart-v2.svc.cluster.local`; the namespace cart-v2 does not exist. The change dropped the Service's cluster IP, and the cluster DNS now answers `cart` with a CNAME to a name that does not resolve. Frontend and checkout kept working on their existing gRPC connections until they were redeployed; every new connection fails, so adding to the cart and checkout fail while the cart pod itself is healthy. The deploys are not the cause.
